claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a solid-solution alloy derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co alters solute–dislocation interactions in FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co reduces the stacking-fault energy.
Reduced stacking-fault energy favors planar slip over cross-slip.
The altered chemical environment in the Co-free alloy promotes planar slip and suppresses cross-slip.
Promotion of planar slip and suppression of cross-slip increase the strain-rate sensitivity of yield strength.
Promotion of planar slip and suppression of cross-slip improve ductility at intermediate temperatures.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, the Co-free alloy will exhibit a greater increase in yield strength as strain rate increases.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, the Co-free alloy will exhibit microstructural evidence of more dominant planar slip.
Dominant planar slip in the Co-free alloy will correlate with improved ductility at intermediate temperatures.
The proposed comparison consists of paired tensile tests on FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under identical temperatures and strain rates.
The proposed regime extends from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures and from quasi-static to moderately high strain rates.
Dislocation mobility predominates over the proposed temperature and strain-rate regime.
The hypothesis applies only in the solid-solution regime where dislocation-mediated plasticity and slip-mode transitions dominate deformation.
The magnitude of the proposed changes in strain-rate sensitivity and ductility may depend on microstructural factors.
